pr.title: Add a work skill that keeps a session working on its own
pr.head: 64c68bd303db6e7537f7cd4484dadeeca4413042

summary: Projector ships its agent workflows as skills: Markdown instructions under skills/ that both Claude Code and Codex load from the same tree. A session left alone with work tends to stop at its first open question and wait for the user, or to keep every pull request in draft until the whole task is done, so nothing is reviewed in the meantime.

This pull request adds a work skill, /projector:work in Claude Code and $work in Codex. It switches the session into working on its own: the session decides what has a reasonable answer, posts what the user must decide to Projector's inbox (the list of questions, requests, and notices that waits above the user's prompt), marks each pull request ready for review as soon as its own work on it is done, and runs fix-pr on each pull request as review events arrive.

The skill adds no code. It cites the sections of implement, fix-pr, and cleanup that already hold the hand-over, event, and subagent rules, rather than restating them. The rest of the change publishes the skill and describes it.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Inbox: the items a session posts for the user with the ask, request, and tell tools in Claude Code, or the project inbox commands elsewhere.
  • Ready: a pull request out of draft. A session that reviews the repository waits until a pull request is ready before it reviews it.
  • Review event: a line such as FINDING or VERDICT that the watch daemon sends a session subscribed to fix a pull request.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, at 64c68bd, requested changes with one finding: on a host without Projector's inbox tools, nothing delivers the user's answers back to the session.
  • The packaging tests, both plugin validations, claude plugin test ., project check, and git diff --check pass at this head.

groups.title: The work skill
groups.kicker: The instructions a session follows to keep working without the user
intro: skills/work/SKILL.md is the whole behavior. It is text an agent follows, so each command and each cited section in it has to match the code and the other skills at this head.
The skill has five parts, in the order a session uses them:

1. Decide what you can. The session answers a choice itself when the request, the repository, or a sensible default answers it. It leaves to the user a product choice, a change of scope, an action that is hard to undo or reaches outside the repository, and declining a person's review finding.
  2. Post what the user must see. Decisions go to ask with a recommendation, work only the user can do goes to request, and news they must act on goes to tell. Where an answer is safe to build on and easy to change, the session builds on its recommendation and says so in the item. It never waits for an answer, and when one arrives it acts on it, undoing work built on a recommendation the user did not pick.
  3. Hand each pull request to review. The session opens each pull request as a draft and marks it ready with project review ready once its own work on it is done.
  4. Fix each pull request as reviews arrive. It runs fix-pr once on each pull request at the start, then again on each review event, in one subagent per pull request.
  5. Keep going until the work is done. It ends a turn only when every piece is done or waits on the user, and then reports its pull requests, decisions, inbox items, and remaining work.

checks.text: The four sections the skill cites exist at this head with those headings: implement "Hand the work over", fix-pr "Give each pull request its own subagent" and "Act on the session's events", and cleanup "Find the session's id". The review read each one against what the skill says about it.

files.note: The new skill: when the session decides, what it posts to the inbox, when it marks a pull request ready, and when it stops.

checks.text: On a host without Projector's inbox tools, such as Codex, the skill posts items with project inbox ask, request, and tell, but names nothing that delivers the user's answers back. Only project inbox watch prints the ANSWER, DONE, and DECLINED lines the next paragraph tells the session to act on, because project watch stream carries only pull request events. A recommendation the user rejects is then never undone. The review asks the skill to name project inbox watch for such a host.

project review ready <number> --repo <owner>/<repo> exists at this head, and marking a finished pull request ready matches the repository's CLAUDE.md under "Hand work over for review". Checked against the command's --help and the head's CLAUDE.md.

The README and docs/plugins.md add the skill to their lists, and docs/plugins.md gains a paragraph on how to start it.
